item.title: Health unit in northwestern Ontario confirms measles case, capping a year of alarming rise in Canadian cases
item.description: The Northwestern Health Unit has confirmed a case of measles in the Kenora area of northwestern Ontario, in a year that saw an alarming rise in cases in Canada and the country lose its measles elimination status.

item.title: Duty free shops say they're still losing sales as Canada-U.S. cross-border travel plummets
item.description: Owners of duty free shops in Windsor and Sarnia say they continue to suffer the fall-out from the U.S. trade war, seeing drops in business in the 30 per cent range year over year.

item.title: Canada, other nations call on Israel to ensure aid groups can work in Gaza

item.title: Father says son killed as Sask. RCMP search for armed pair on Big Island Lake Cree Nation
item.description: At least one man is dead and police are searching for two armed men on Big Island Lake Cree Nation, CBC News has learned. Saskatchewan RCMP are telling people living on the First Nation near the Alberta border to find a safe location immediately and lock their doors.

item.title: Pimicikamak Cree Nation declares state of emergency after power outage in northern Manitoba
item.description: Residents of a northern Manitoba First Nation are being told that their power will not be restored until late in the day on New Year’s Eve. Pimicikamak Cree Nation declared a state of emergency on Monday following a widespread power outage in the Cross Lake area around 11:30 p.m. Sunday.

item.title: What's coming up next in Canadian politics? Here are five key stories to watch in 2026
item.description: 2026 is shaping up to be an action-packed year in Canadian politics. Federal opposition parties will make key decisions on their futures as the Liberal government, just one seat shy of a majority government, strategizes what to do next while juggling U.S. trade talks. Here are five key stories to keep an eye on next year.
